answer: Within one epoch, answers whose 64-bit SimHash over word 3-grams differ in at most 8 bits form a reef; the earliest member, the basalt anchor, keeps full weight and the k-th member gets 1/k. An operator submitting 200 paraphrases through 200 identities earns H_200 ≈ 5.9 weights, not 200. Weakness: an LLM rewrite that moves more than 8 bits costs cents per identity, so the cheapest bypass is linear but no longer free, and honest collisions lose at worst a nadir of 1/k.
